transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-29 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Tom Blake (Ivy - Head of ML), Sarah Patel (Ivy - Platform Eng), Priya Rao (Ivy - CFO)

Summary: Short discovery to understand Ivy's budget constraints, latency targets, and to scope a pilot that compares Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated with security/residency requirements. Discussed per-token economics, batching and caching levers, and pilot success metrics.

Topics: cost per token, batching, prefix/KV caching, dedicated capacity pricing, private/VPC options, SOC2/KMS, pilot scope & benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Maya, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Maya: hey all, hi. quick note I'm gonna dig into perf/cost questions.
[00:15] Tom: Tom here — head of ML at Ivy. We're evaluating where to host, cost is a big gating factor, also we can't exceed about 200ms p95 for user-facing prompts.
[00:25] Priya: Priya, CFO, i'm mostly interested in cost predictability and any hidden fees - like storage or egress — and compliance posture.
[00:32] Sarah: Sarah, platform eng. i'll own infra requirements and SSO/KMS integration if we move forward.
[00:37] Alex: Great. the goal today: walk through unit economics, show levers you can pull (batching, caching, quantization) and then sketch a pilot that proves out both cost and latency.
[00:47] Tom: sounds good. quick context: we have approx 500k user interactions/day, average prompt+response ~180 tokens combined, critical prompts are under 128 tokens but many followups add up.
[00:58] Maya: ok so ballpark tokens/day is 90M (500k * 180) — if we estimate per-token hosted price at say $0.000003 (example) that's about $270/month just raw generation cost — wait, math-check, actually that would be $270/day, sorry i munged the numbers — yes we should clarify units.
[01:20] Priya: yeah please be explicit per-month budgets. our initial annual budget for inference is roughly $600k/year (~$50k/month) for all AI infra.
[01:30] Alex: helpful. to be clear, hosted pricing is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with a fixed monthly commit and lower per-token execution cost.
[01:40] Maya: also we can cut tokens by two main levers: prefix/KV caching for repeated context (we've seen 20-60% token reductions depending on UX), and batching on the runtime which reduces per-token kernel overhead.
[01:54] Tom: how does batching affect latency? our p95 requirement worries me, we can't add large tail latency.
[01:59] Maya: good question. continuous batching is latency-aware — it will group short windows of requests up to a configured threshold. for p95 sensitive traffic you'd set a small max-wait (like 5-10ms) and let the engine do micro-batches, which still gives some efficiency. bigger batches (50-100ms wait) improve throughput but increase tail. so it's a tradeoff.
[02:20] Sarah: what about KV cache? our app has a lot of repeated system prompts and docs per user. can that be pinned?
[02:26] Maya: yeah prefix/KV caching lets you cache tokenized key-value states for repeated prefixes. typical embed-and-lookup patterns can avoid re-sending the same prompt content, saving upstream tokens and latency. we also have configurable cache TTLs.
[02:36] Priya: any numbers on how caching translates to $ saved?
[02:40] Maya: rough example: if caching reduces token volume by 40%, that 90M/day becomes 54M/day. per-token execution charge drops proportionally, plus you'll reduce network egress in hosted mode. so with a $0.000003/token example, you'd go from $270/day to $162/day. but again that's an illustrative price, we'll send exact host/dedicated examples.
[03:02] Tom: ok but those per-token numbers seem lower than vendors we've seen — can you show hosted vs dedicated breakouts?
[03:08] Alex: yes we'll send a spreadsheet. typical pattern: hosted per-token is highest but zero commit; dedicated has a monthly base (e.g., $Xk/mo for a pool of GPUs) plus lower per-token compute fees and predictable throughput. for customers with steady volume, dedicated gives better unit economics.
[03:24] Tom: and private / VPC — is that a flat premium on top?
[03:28] Maya: Private/VPC has a platform fee and possibly infra add-ons for on-prem. If you need HSM/KMS in customer control, there's integration work and additional sysadmin overhead; pricing depends on the deployment model.
[03:41] Priya: we need SOC 2 and data residency in EU for European users, and KMS that we control. that's non-negotiable.
[03:48] Alex: Redwood supports SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer encryption at rest and bring-your-own-key options in some tiers but can discuss details. we'll attach security docs.
[03:58] Sarah: network egress — if we host in eu-west, does Redwood charge egress back to our cloud?
[04:04] Maya: hosted egress is included for typical use but there can be interoperability egress if you route cross-cloud. we'll note region-specific considerations in the sheet.
[04:12] Tom: let's talk concrete pilot scope. what do we need to validate?
[04:16] Alex: i'd propose a 4-week pilot: 1) run a perf/cost benchmark on a representative set of 2k prompts (we'll test hosted and dedicated configurations), 2) instrument KV/prefix caching on a subset of traffic to estimate token reduction, 3) measure p50/p95 latency under realistic concurrency, 4) surface a cost model for 3 traffic scenarios (baseline, optimized-caching, high-growth).
[04:39] Priya: what would that pilot cost look like? we have to work within the $50k/month target.
[04:44] Maya: pilots are typically low-cost; for example, we can offer Hosted trial credits for the benchmark and run Dedicated as a temporary reserved pool at reduced pilot rate. rough pilot budget could be $5-15k depending on scale — we'll baseline it and send options.
[05:00] Tom: can you run the dedicated config on our region? latency matters.
[05:04] Maya: yes we can colocate dedicated pools in region; for private deployments we can deploy into your VPC as well. there are lead times for on-prem but cloud VPC is faster.
[05:12] Sarah: about instrumentation — do you expose token-level traces? we need to map costs to routes.
[05:18] Alex: Console shows token-level cost and latency by route, model, and token type. we can produce per-route cost breakdowns for your routes and tie them to a cost center.
[05:27] Tom: any concerns about quality differences if we quantize to save cost?
[05:31] Maya: model quantization can change quality slightly; we provide recommended quantization profiles and we can A/B test with rollouts. typical GPT-like family quantization at 4-bit is often fine for many use cases, but we'll run quality checks against your eval set.
[05:45] Priya: do you bill for cache storage or only tokens?
[05:48] Alex: cache storage in Hosted may have a small storage fee for long-term prefixes, but usually it's minimal relative to token costs. Dedicated includes caching as part of the runtime. we'll call out any storage line items in the spreadsheet.
[05:59] Tom: what's the SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[06:03] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency/uptime guarantees; Hosted has uptime SLAs at tenant-level and best-effort latency tiers. we'll include specifics per plan in the doc.
[06:13] Sarah: security — if we go private with our KMS, is Redwood's control plane still talking to your cloud? we want to minimize data leaving our VPC.
[06:20] Maya: with Private you can have a customer-managed control plane and the runtime in your VPC — REDACTED (note: internal naming), so logs can be exported to your SIEM and the control-plane calls are minimized. we'll share architecture diagrams.
[06:33] Alex: ok i want to do a back-of-envelope for monthly spend if you scale to 1.5M interactions/day. with current 180 tokens avg that's 270M tokens/day. with hosted at $0.000003/token that's $810/day or ~$24k/month — again placeholder numbers. with 40% caching you get to $14.4k/month. but dedicated at scale might bring per-token to $0.0000015 plus a base pool fee which could be more predictable within your $50k/month ceiling.
[07:03] Priya: that math helps. we also care about peak capacity — some days spike 3x. how do you handle spikes?
[07:09] Maya: we offer burst policies on Dedicated that use leftover capacity or hosted fallback; routing policies can send overflow to hosted to avoid throttling. that does change economics because bursts are billed at hosted rates unless you have idle dedicated headroom.
[07:24] Tom: is there a way to throttle or route lower-priority traffic to cheaper model variants?
[07:28] Maya: yes, smart routing can tier by cost/latency — critical traffic pins to low-latency model on dedicated, non-critical to cheaper model or quantized variant.
[07:36] Sarah: for the perf benchmark — what metrics do you collect?
[07:40] Maya: p50/p90/p95 latency, tokens produced, GPU utilization, effective batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, and cost per generated token. we'll package results and suggestions (batching windows, cache TTLs, quantization profile).
[07:53] Tom: timeline — if we decide to pilot, when can it start?
[07:57] Alex: we can kick off in ~2 weeks after a quick scoping doc and an NDA (if needed). pilot itself 3-4 weeks once we have eval prompts.
[08:06] Priya: legal — we have procurement cycles, requires SOC2 & DPA review. can you provide those before we sign pilot?
[08:13] Alex: yes, we'll attach SOC 2 docs, DPA template, and a sample pilot contract.
[08:18] Sarah: cross-cloud egress question again — if our data plane is in GCP and Redwood hosted is in AWS in eu-west, does that incur egress?
[08:26] Maya: cross-cloud will imply egress; best is to choose matching region or host in your VPC. we'll call out egress scenarios in the cost model.
[08:35] Tom: can you include examples of customers similar to us who moved from hosted to dedicated and achieved savings?
[08:40] Alex: yes we'll include anonymized case studies.
[08:42] Tom: any limitations on model versions on Dedicated?
[08:45] Maya: You can pin model versions. some experimental model variants may not be available immediately on Dedicated, but we can prioritize onboarding for pilots.
[08:55] Priya: one more cost question: are there minimum commitments?
[08:58] Alex: Dedicated has minimum commit terms (monthly) but pilot can be done with reduced-term trial pools. Hosted has no commit.
[09:05] Sarah: will you provide a route-level per-token cost that maps to our product features?
[09:10] Maya: yes, that's part of the deliverable — per-route cost, suggestions for routing and caching to hit cost targets.
[09:16] Tom: ok let's move to wrap-up and next steps.
[09:19] Alex: Recap: we'll send a cost-model spreadsheet with hosted/dedicated/private examples, include egress and cache storage notes; Maya will run a 2k prompt perf/cost benchmark for hosted and a dedicated temp pool; Priya will review security docs and provide SOC2/KMS contacts; customer to confirm 2k prompt set and success criteria.
[09:39] Priya: timeline — i can get you SOC contact and a first pass on budget constraints by Wed (2026-11-04).
[09:46] Tom: i'll pick the 2k prompt set and share with Maya by next Tue (2026-11-03).
[09:52] Alex: perfect. we'll set up a follow-up in ~10 days to review benchmark results and cost model.
[10:00] Maya: any final questions?
[10:03] Sarah: just to confirm — you'll include a sample routing policy that tiers traffic?
[10:07] Maya: yes, sample routing and batching configs will be in the doc.
[10:11] Alex: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for the bench review.
[10:18] Tom: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had occasional speaker swaps and word errors (times/cost numbers reviewed and corrected by AE).
